name: Carlos Ghosn
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Michelin in 1978 at age 24 as a trainee; became plant manager at Le Puy in 1981 at age 27. Major leadership roles (COO Michelin South America, CEO Michelin North America, Nissan COO) all came after age 30. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Porto Velho, Brazil to a Lebanese family, Ghosn moved to Beirut at age six and later to France for his education. He graduated from École Polytechnique and École des Mines de Paris in 1978 and joined Michelin as a trainee at age 24.
family_context_summary: Born to a Lebanese family in Porto Velho, Brazil; grandfather emigrated from Lebanon at age 13. Family moved to Beirut when Ghosn was six.
evidence_summary: Ghosn graduated from elite French engineering schools (École Polytechnique, École des Mines) and joined Michelin at 24, but his first promotion to plant manager came at 27. His career-defining achievements — restructuring Michelin North America, turning around Nissan — all occurred well after age 30. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Toyo Ito
milestone_by_age_26: Graduated from University of Tokyo in 1965 at age 24 and worked as an apprentice at Kiyonori Kikutake's firm. Started his own studio (Urban Robot) in 1971 at age 30. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Seoul (then Japanese Korea) to Japanese parents, Ito moved to Japan in 1943. He graduated from the University of Tokyo's architecture department in 1965 and apprenticed under Kiyonori Kikutake, a founder of the Metabolist Movement, for four years before establishing his own studio in 1971.
family_context_summary: Born to a Japanese family in Seoul; father was a businessman and chairman of a textile subsidiary of Mitsui & Co. Father died when Ito was 12, after which the family operated a miso factory.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a businessman with interest in early Korean ceramic ware; grandfather was a lumber dealer. Mother commissioned an architect to design their Tokyo home, exposing Ito to architecture.
evidence_summary: Ito graduated from the University of Tokyo in 1965 at 24 and apprenticed under Kiyonori Kikutake until 1969. He founded his own studio in 1971 at age 30. His first notable built works came in the early 1970s, well after age 26. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Brad Pitt
milestone_by_age_26: Began acting in 1987 at age 24 with uncredited extra roles and TV guest spots. First film to reach theaters was Cutting Class (1989) at age 25, a minor horror film. Breakthrough came with Thelma & Louise in 1991 at age 27. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Shawnee, Oklahoma and raised in Missouri, Pitt studied journalism at the University of Missouri before dropping out two credits short of graduation to move to Los Angeles. He took acting lessons and supported himself with odd jobs while landing small TV roles starting in 1987.
family_context_summary: Son of a trucking company manager, raised in a strict Baptist household in Missouri as the oldest of three children.
evidence_summary: Pitt moved to Los Angeles after leaving college and began taking acting classes. His early career consisted of uncredited film extras, TV guest appearances (Dallas, 21 Jump Street), and a Pringles commercial. His first leading film role (The Dark Side of the Sun, 1988) was shelved and not released until 1997. His breakthrough role in Thelma & Louise came in 1991 at age 27. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Arata Isozaki

family_context_summary: Born in Oita, Kyushu; father was a prominent businessman. Grew up in the era of postwar Japan, witnessing the destruction of Hiroshima from across the shore.

name: Johan Museeuw
milestone_by_age_26: Won two prestigious stages at the 1990 Tour de France at age 24, including the uphill-sprint stage to Mont Saint-Michel and the final stage on the Champs-Élysées in Paris.
early_history_summary: Born in Varsenare and raised in Gistel, West Flanders, Museeuw grew up in a cycling family — his father Eddy rode professionally for two seasons. He focused on cyclo-cross as a junior, becoming Belgian junior champion, before turning professional with ADR in 1988 at age 22. By 1990, he had won two stages at the Tour de France.
family_context_summary: Born to Eddy Museeuw, a former professional cyclist who quit after two seasons to become a motor mechanic, and raised in Gistel, West Flanders — a town in the heartland of Flemish cycling culture.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Eddy was a professional cyclist for two seasons and later a motor mechanic; he guided Johan's early cycling career and offered the family garage business as a fallback.
primary_early_advantage_tags: cycling family, Flemish cycling culture, cyclo-cross junior champion, professional team at 22
evidence_summary: Museeuw grew up in Gistel, West Flanders, the heartland of Flemish cycling, with a father who had ridden professionally. He specialized in cyclo-cross as a junior, becoming Belgian junior champion, before turning professional with ADR in 1988. By 1990, at age 24, he won two prestigious stages at the Tour de France, including the final stage in Paris. His father's cycling background and the immersive Flemish cycling culture provided direct domain exposure from childhood, while the ADR team environment connected him to elite international racing.
starting_point: Born to a middle-class family in Varsenare, Belgium; father was a former professional cyclist turned motor mechanic, raised in the cycling heartland of West Flanders.
current_position: Retired from professional cycling in 2004; active as a cycling ambassador and public figure in Belgium.

name: Joseph Tsai
milestone_by_age_26: Earned JD from Yale Law School in 1990 at age 26 and began as a tax associate at Sullivan & Cromwell. Co-founded Alibaba in 1999 at age 35. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Taipei, Taiwan to a second-generation lawyer, Tsai was sent to the U.S. at age 13 to attend the Lawrenceville School. He earned a BA from Yale in 1986 and a JD from Yale Law School in 1990, then worked as a tax associate at Sullivan & Cromwell before moving to private equity and eventually co-founding Alibaba in 1999.
family_context_summary: Born to Paul C. Tsai, a second-generation lawyer, and Ruby Tsai in Taipei, Taiwan. Sent to the U.S. at age 13 for boarding school. Father attended Yale University.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a second-generation lawyer and Yale alumnus; family had legal profession background.
evidence_summary: Tsai earned his Yale BA in 1986 and JD in 1990, then worked as a tax associate at Sullivan & Cromwell and later in private equity at Investor AB. His career-defining achievement — co-founding Alibaba with Jack Ma — came in 1999 at age 35. By age 26, he had just completed his law degree and started as an associate. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Björk
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut album 'Life's Too Good' with the Sugarcubes in April 1988 at age 22, achieving international chart success and critical acclaim as the band's lead singer.
early_history_summary: Born in Reykjavík, Björk began studying piano and flute at the Barnamúsíkskóli music school at age six. After a recording of her singing was broadcast on national radio, she released a self-titled album at age 11. She spent her teen years in anarchist punk bands including KUKL before forming the Sugarcubes in 1986, whose 1988 debut album brought international fame.
family_context_summary: Raised by her mother Hildur Rúna Hauksdóttir, an activist, in a commune in Reykjavík after her parents divorced. Her stepfather Sævar Árnason was a guitarist in the band Pops, providing a musical environment. Biological father was an electrician and union leader.
parent_family_domain_summary: Stepfather Sævar Árnason was a guitarist in the band Pops, exposing Björk to music from an early age. Mother was an activist who supported her musical education.
primary_early_advantage_tags: music school from age 6, musician stepfather, child album at 11, punk band teens, Icelandic post-punk scene
evidence_summary: Björk's musical path began at age six at the Barnamúsíkskóli music school in Reykjavík, leading to a radio broadcast and a self-titled album at age 11. Her stepfather, a guitarist, provided a musical household. After teen years in punk bands including KUKL, she formed the Sugarcubes in 1986. Their 1988 debut album 'Life's Too Good' achieved international chart success and critical acclaim, with Björk's distinctive three-octave vocals as the standout element. The combination of early music education, family musical environment, and intensive early practice from age six drove her breakthrough by age 22.
starting_point: Born to a working-class family in Reykjavík, Iceland; father was an electrician and union leader, mother an activist; parents divorced when she was young, and she was raised in a commune with her mother and musician stepfather.
current_position: Active recording artist and performer; released latest album 'Fossora' in 2022; resides in Reykjavík, Iceland; regarded as one of the most influential musicians of her era.

Starred in and scored the film 'Dancer in the Dark', winning the Best Actress award at the Cannes Film Festival.
Released 'Fossora', her tenth studio album and first venture as sole producer.

name: Oleg Goncharenko
milestone_by_age_26: Became World Allround Speed Skating Champion in Helsinki in 1953 at age 21, the first Soviet male speed skater to win the world championship title.
early_history_summary: Born in Kharkiv, Ukraine, Goncharenko lost his father during World War II and developed his skating skills largely through self-training, using physical labor such as firewood chopping and railroad car unloading as conditioning. He graduated from the Kharkiv Fire Technical School in 1952, competed for the Dynamo sports society, and made his international debut in 1953, immediately winning the World Allround Championship at age 21.
family_context_summary: Born in Kharkiv, Ukrainian SSR; father was lost during World War II. Grew up in post-war Soviet Ukraine in modest circumstances, largely self-trained before entering the Soviet sports system.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Father was lost during WWII; no details about his occupation or athletic background found.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-trained, WWII adversity, Dynamo sports society, Soviet sports system, natural talent
evidence_summary: Goncharenko grew up in war-torn Kharkiv, losing his father during World War II. Without formal coaching initially, he developed his own training methods using physical labor as conditioning. After graduating from the Kharkiv Fire Technical School in 1952, he entered the Dynamo sports society under coaches V. Zhelubovsky and K. Kudryavtsev, and made his international debut in 1953, immediately winning the World Allround Championship in Helsinki at age 21 — the first Soviet male speed skater to achieve this. His trajectory reflects a combination of natural talent, self-driven training, and the Soviet sports system's infrastructure.
starting_point: Born in Kharkiv, Ukrainian SSR, to a family that lost its father during World War II; grew up in post-war Soviet Ukraine in modest circumstances.
current_position: Died in 1986 in Moscow at age 55; final role: coach of the Soviet youth speed skating team after retiring from competition in 1962.

name: René Fasel
milestone_by_age_26: Played amateur hockey for HC Fribourg-Gottéron until 1972 at age 22, then became a referee. Became president of the Swiss Ice Hockey Federation in 1985 at age 35 and IIHF President in 1994. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Fribourg, Switzerland, Fasel played for HC Fribourg-Gottéron in the amateur division from 1960 to 1972. He retired from playing at 22 to become a referee, officiating 37 international matches until 1982. He graduated as a dentist in 1977 and practiced dentistry for 17 years before moving into hockey administration full-time.
family_context_summary: Born in Fribourg, Switzerland; trained as a dentist, practicing for 17 years alongside his hockey involvement.
evidence_summary: Fasel played amateur hockey and then became a referee in his early twenties. He graduated as a dentist in 1977 and practiced for 17 years. His hockey administration career began in 1982 as chairman of the Swiss referees' commission, and he became president of the Swiss Ice Hockey Federation in 1985 at age 35. His defining role as IIHF President came in 1994 at age 44. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Anna Muzychuk
milestone_by_age_26: Awarded the FIDE Grandmaster title in 2012 at age 21, becoming the fourth woman in chess history to reach a 2600 Elo rating, and won the Women's World Blitz Chess Championship in 2014 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Born in Lviv, Ukraine to parents who are both professional chess coaches, Muzychuk learned chess at age two and began competing at five. She won the European Youth Championship at age six and was homeschooled to allow more time for chess. She earned the IM title at 17, won the World Junior Championship at 20, and became a Grandmaster at 21 — the fourth woman to cross 2600 Elo.
family_context_summary: Born to Oleh and Nataliya Muzychuk, both professional chess coaches who studied coaching at the Lviv State Institute of Physical Culture. Her younger sister Mariya also became a chess Grandmaster and Women's World Champion.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents are professional chess coaches who taught Anna and her sister Mariya chess from age two, homeschooled Anna to maximize chess training time, and studied coaching at the Lviv State Institute of Physical Culture.
primary_early_advantage_tags: chess coach parents, homeschooled for chess, sister GM, prodigy from age 2, Slovenian federation support
evidence_summary: Muzychuk's chess career was built on an extraordinary family-domain apprenticeship: both parents are professional chess coaches who taught her the game at age two and homeschooled her to maximize training time. She won the European Youth Championship at six, earned the IM title at 17, won the World Junior Championship at 20, and became a Grandmaster at 21 — the fourth woman to reach 2600 Elo. Her sister Mariya also became a GM and Women's World Champion, creating a high-trust peer environment. The depth of parental coaching and total immersion in chess from toddlerhood represent exceptionally strong early advantages.

current_position: Active chess Grandmaster; ranked among the world's top women players; represents Ukraine in international competition.

name: Viorica Viscopoleanu
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Romanian national long jump championship in 1962 at age 23, beginning a streak of nine consecutive national titles, and finished 5th at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born in Storozhynets (then Kingdom of Romania, now Ukraine), Viscopoleanu lost her mother at age five and was raised by grandparents. During World War II, her family fled to Bucharest as refugees. She initially pursued volleyball and gymnastics before being steered toward athletics by a school sports teacher, where she was discovered by coach Ion Vintila and later joined Steaua Bucharest under coach Ion Soter.
family_context_summary: Born in Storozhynets, Kingdom of Romania (now Ukraine); lost her mother at age five and was raised by grandparents. The family fled as refugees to Bucharest during World War II, settling in modest circumstances.
primary_early_advantage_tags: war refugee, Steaua Bucharest, Romanian sports system, coach Ion Soter, perseverance
evidence_summary: Viscopoleanu's early life was marked by adversity: she lost her mother at age five, was raised by grandparents, and fled as a refugee to Bucharest during World War II. She initially pursued volleyball and gymnastics before being steered toward athletics by a school sports teacher and discovered by coach Ion Vintila. Joining Steaua Bucharest under coach Ion Soter provided access to Romania's elite sports infrastructure. By 1962, at age 23, she was Romanian national long jump champion, and at 25 she finished 5th at the Tokyo Olympics. Her trajectory reflects perseverance through hardship and the support of the Romanian state sports system.
starting_point: Born in Storozhynets, Kingdom of Romania (now Ukraine), to a family that lost its mother when Viorica was five; raised by grandparents and later became a wartime refugee fleeing to Bucharest.
current_position: Retired; former athletics coach at Steaua Bucharest; residing in Romania as of 2025 at age 86.
